author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
Voluntary health insurance concerns the medical services included in the selected programme, within the contract's limits. For an individual or company in the Republic of Moldova, comparison starts with services and access, not a promise that every consultation is free. The clinic name, annual amount and policy price do not sufficiently explain accepted costs and remaining payments.

This material explains comparison preparation and documents to check. It does not recommend examinations or treatment, or confirm a programme for every applicant. Medical decisions belong to healthcare professionals. Insurance ING Broker SRL explains and brokers available options; acceptance, conditions and expenditure decisions belong to the insurer under the contract.

The medical programme matters more than the package name

Request the service list in the version accompanying the contract. Distinguish consultations, tests, outpatient treatment, hospitalisation and additional services. These categories are assessment questions, not a universal coverage list. Each may have different rules, and a short online presentation does not replace the insured person's applicable programme.

Read the footnotes. An annual amount may coexist with separate limits, visit numbers or conditions for particular services. Ask for administrative examples: making an appointment, checking the request and receiving documents. A service offered commercially by a clinic is not necessarily included in the policy. Compare the clinic and service lists together.

Do not confuse voluntary cover with the mandatory system

Voluntary and mandatory health insurance have different documents and mechanisms. Buying a private programme does not establish that every requirement concerning mandatory insurance status has been met. Check CNAM information and the person's circumstances for those questions. This article does not determine an applicant's legal status or assess their obligations.

Ask which documents are used to access each service. Keep voluntary policy details separate from documents requested by the medical institution. If an employer provides a staff benefit, explain the difference in a simple internal guide. Avoid saying no other insurance is needed without a review applicable to that person and situation.

Check the network by service and location

A large network does not by itself solve access where you live or work. Request the current list and check relevant institutions. Go beyond a hospital name: ask which programme services can be accessed there and how. Some administrative questions need an answer from the insurer, clinic or assistance company.

For teams across several districts, prepare a location list without personal medical information. A programme selected solely for access in Chișinău may be difficult for employees elsewhere. Ask about available alternatives and procedures if a provider changes. Do not promise equal appointment availability at every institution.

Direct booking and approval are different steps

Clarify whether you can call the clinic directly, must contact an assistance centre or should follow another programme route. Check what information is needed before a consultation. A reception booking is not acceptance of expenditure by the insurer. Administrative confirmation should concern the particular service, person and documents.

Record the urgent-care procedure separately. Do not delay necessary medical help to compare policies or read this article. Assistance and contractual checks are coordinated according to circumstances and competent instructions. This material does not decide whether a condition is a medical emergency or replace emergency services and a doctor's assessment.

Direct payment and reimbursement work differently

Ask who pays for the service and which records support any refund. Direct payment to a provider and reimbursement of personal expenditure may involve different steps. Request the documents, relevant form and submission channel. Do not assume every receipt presented afterwards must be accepted regardless of the programme, procedure or service.

Keep medical and financial records securely with restricted access. Do not send them to an employer or broker merely because they helped choose the policy. Ask who needs each document and why. An initial commercial enquiry does not require publishing a diagnosis or medical history in an open form.

Read limits and personal cost contributions

A premium is the amount paid for insurance. An excess or deductible is the portion of a loss borne by the insured under the contract. If the programme uses other contributions, request billing examples rather than assuming all policies use the same terms. Check whether a limit is annual, per service or defined another way.

Compare proposals for the same person or employee category. A cheaper programme may have a different network, service list or limits. That does not automatically make it unsuitable; understand differences before choosing. A higher premium does not prove that every medical need is included either. Keep unanswered questions in the comparison table.

Discuss known conditions and exclusions confidentially

Exclusions are situations for which the contract provides no cover. Read how existing illnesses or circumstances, planned services and treatment already started are described. Do not conceal legitimately requested information or alter answers to make acceptance seem easier. Ask when a question is unclear and use the specified confidential channel.

Do not extrapolate one programme's condition to the whole market. A heading called “investigations” does not confirm every procedure or recommendation. Check the actual service in policy documents. Medical interpretation of health and contractual assessment of expenditure are different matters. The broker cannot replace a doctor or promise an insurer's decision.

What an employer should check before including the team

Define staff categories and joining or leaving arrangements. Ask about new colleagues, departures, name changes and family members if relevant. Do not send a larger personnel database than necessary. Separate benefit administration from access to individual medical files. The person maintaining staff lists should not be presented as a diagnosis assessor.

Prepare a guide containing policy contacts, booking steps and where to find the programme. Avoid promises about treatment, guaranteed waiting times or universal reimbursement. Obtain specialist advice on tax and employment questions. An insurer's public programme description does not automatically certify the tax treatment of your company's benefit.

A comparison example without invented amounts

A Moldovan company considers two employee programmes. The first has institutions near the office, while the second offers a different service list. The administrator compares locations, access procedures and limits separately instead of relying only on annual premium. This is an editorial example, not an actual customer or recommendation of a particular insurer.

An approval question remains unclear in the table. The company obtains an answer before announcing the benefit. A service is marked included only from programme documents, not because a partner clinic has the necessary machine. Staff communication stays tied to confirmed records. Final selection depends on actual needs and conditions, not a universal ranking for every business.

A simple programme comparison sheet

Create a working page for each option. Record its name, document version and response date, followed by relevant locations, services and access arrangements. For every answer, identify its source: programme, conditions, schedule or written clarification. Another person can then check the comparison without interpreting a telephone conversation.

Include waiting periods where stated, booking arrangements, validity of approvals and invoice submission. Do not enter “yes” because another programme had that feature. If the insurer needs more information, keep the condition unconfirmed pending an answer. A short accurate document is more useful than a lengthy description mixing different offers.

Finally, explain in everyday language what a beneficiary should do before a planned visit and which records to keep afterwards. Check whether the steps make sense without insurance terminology. Do not promise that following them guarantees payment: the sheet provides administrative clarity. For a change or renewal, recheck details instead of automatically sending last year's guide.

Frequently asked questions about private medical insurance

Can I attend any private clinic?

Check your programme's network and procedure. A private institution or its presence in a general presentation does not confirm every service is accepted. Seek clarification before planned expenditure, following the contractual procedure.

How much does a health programme cost?

Request assessment of the services, people and institutions concerned. This article has no confirmed tariff for every enquiry. Compare cost alongside limits, exclusions and actual access.

Are hospitalisation and preventive check-ups included automatically?

Do not assume so. Find the services in the programme and check their separate rules. A general package name does not confirm payment for an admission or test panel.

What information should I send initially?

Your needs, locations and beneficiary categories are a useful start. Then request the exact list and submission channel. Do not upload medical histories, identity documents or employee files to a general public enquiry.
